item.title: Running the 2025 Annual Disaster Recovery Exercise
item.description:
Annual DR exercise for a customer with strict compliance requirements (SOC 2). Copy representative data to an isolated environment, failover to the DR site, run a full smoke test against the failed-over setup.

Running this for the second year in a row meant comparing against last time - what was slower than expected, what documentation was wrong, where the runbook needed updates. If each iteration of an annual DR exercise doesn’t make you faster and more confident, it’s just checking a compliance box, not actually improving your recovery posture.

item.title: Running an Annual Disaster Recovery Exercise for a Compliance-Driven Customer
item.description:
Regulated customers (financial services, etc.) need documented proof that disaster recovery actually works, not just exists on paper. Annual DR exercise to satisfy that requirement.

Copy representative data to an isolated recovery environment, failover to the DR site, smoke test critical functionality. Coordinating with the customer on what data’s usable and hitting their testing window is as much the project as the technical failover.

Running it annually instead of only when disaster strikes is what makes the DR plan credible instead of theoretical.
